hero.headline: Congress returns to unresolved immigration and Iran oversight disputes
hero.teaser: Lawmakers face the same stalled issues they left before the holiday break.
hero.body:
Congress returns with immigration funding, a Justice Department fund dispute, and Iran war oversight questions still unresolved. Lawmakers left for Memorial Day break without making progress on any of the three issues.

The immigration enforcement funding package remains stalled. Questions about congressional oversight of the Iran war also await resolution when members return to Washington.

cards.headline: Israel captures Beaufort Castle in expanded Lebanon offensive
cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized the historic fortress in southern Lebanon as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a deeper ground operation against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with northern Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu characterized the seizure as a "decisive shift" in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah, stating that "we returned stronger than ever."

The castle holds deep symbolic weight for both nations. Israel previously occupied the strategic position during its extended military presence in southern Lebanon. The current capture suggests Israel intends to maintain an extended presence in the region as its offensive expands.

cards.headline: Israel captures castle in Lebanon as ground offensive expands
cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized a strategic fortress in Lebanon during an expanding military campaign against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured the 12th-century Beaufort Castle, a strategic fortress overlooking southern Lebanon and northern Israel, as part of an expanding ground offensive against Hezbollah. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the seizure as a "decisive shift" in the military campaign.

The operation signals Israel's intention to maintain an extended military presence in Lebanon. The castle capture marks an escalation of Israeli ground operations in the region.

cards.headline: U.S.-Iran conflict reaches Sri Lankan town in deadly strike
cards.teaser: A strike during the opening days of the Iran war hit a town on the Indian Ocean, demonstrating the geographic range of the conflict.
cards.body:
A deadly military strike connected to the U.S.-Iran war struck a seaside town in Sri Lanka during the first days of the conflict. The attack reached far into the Indian Ocean, hitting the quiet coastal community.

The strike jolted the town and illustrated how widely the conflict between the United States and Iran has spread beyond the two countries. The war's reach has extended across a significant geographic area including regions far from the primary combatants.

cards.headline: U.S. military strikes alleged drug boat in Pacific, killing 3 in fourth attack this week
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out another strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Saturday, killing three people. This marks the second strike in as many days and the fourth attack this week, according to officials with U.S. Southern Command.

Military officials said intelligence confirmed the vessel was traveling along routes typically used for drug trafficking in the eastern Pacific and was engaged in narco-trafficking operations. The strike adds to a mounting death toll from a broader campaign targeting boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific that has killed at least 205 people since last September.

The campaign has generated significant controversy. Legal experts and civil rights organizations have challenged the strikes as violations of both domestic and international law. The families of two men from Trinidad killed in a previous strike have filed a lawsuit against the government.

The Trump administration has defended the military campaign as lawful, arguing the United States is at war with drug cartels and therefore adhering to the laws of conflict. Officials have framed the strikes as necessary to prevent overdose deaths in America and stop the flow of illicit drugs into the country. "What we're doing is actually an act of kindness," Trump said last year regarding the strikes.

However, the evidence supporting military claims that targeted vessels are involved in drug trafficking has been limited. The U.S. Southern Command has released a steady stream of social media posts announcing the strikes, typically accompanied by low-resolution videos showing vessels being destroyed.

UN officials have described the U.S. campaign as a flagrant violation of human rights. Civil rights groups have committed to challenging the strikes through all available legal pathways. Jamil Dakwar, director of the American Civil Rights Union's Human Rights Program, stated that the organization is "doing everything in our power to hold the Trump administration responsible for its egregious violations of both U.S. and international law," including requesting that the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights investigate the killings.

The Pacific Ocean has long served as a transit route for drug trafficking operations moving narcotics from South American production areas toward North American markets. The U.S. military and Coast Guard regularly patrol these waters as part of counter-narcotics efforts. However, the frequency and intensity of strikes this week represent a significant escalation in the use of direct military force in what has traditionally been primarily a law enforcement mission.

The strikes continue as the Trump administration pursues its counter-narcotics strategy in maritime regions, though the campaign remains contentious among international observers and human rights advocates.

cards.headline: U.S. Military Guides Commercial Ships Through Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced a new initiative called Project Freedom to assist commercial vessels navigating through the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating regional tensions. Trump stated that the operation would represent a humanitarian effort "on behalf of the United States, Middle Eastern Countries but, in particular, the Country of Iran."

U.S. Central Command has already helped approximately 70 commercial ships transit the strait over a three-week period. The military assistance addresses growing security concerns as tensions in the Middle East continue to disrupt maritime commerce in one of the world's most critical shipping channels.

The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, serving as a passage for roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies. At its narrowest point, the waterway measures only 21 miles wide, making it a strategic chokepoint for global energy markets. Major oil producers including Saudi Arabia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, and Iraq depend on the strait to export crude oil to international markets.

The U.S. government has not disclosed specific details about the nature of the assistance provided or the duration of the escort operations. The disclosure of the assistance effort signals the administration's commitment to maintaining freedom of navigation in the region's waters.

However, the initiative faces significant resistance from Iran. The head of the Iranian military's unified command warned that U.S. and foreign armed forces would face attacks if they enter the strait. Iranian military officials told U.S. forces to remain out of the area and stated they would respond harshly to any perceived threat. Iran also instructed commercial ships and oil tankers to avoid any movement without coordination with Iranian military authorities.

Trump indicated that his representatives were having "very positive" discussions with Iran and instructed them to inform Iranian officials that the U.S. would make "best efforts to get their Ships and Crews safely out of the Strait."

The shipping lane's importance to global commerce means that disruptions can quickly affect energy prices and supply chains worldwide. Any sustained interruption in traffic through the strait could create significant economic consequences internationally.

Central Command oversees U.S. military operations across the Middle East and parts of Central and South Asia. Officials have not specified whether the assistance to approximately 70 ships over three weeks represents an increase in escort activity compared to previous operations or reflects continuation of existing protocols.

The military operation represents a quiet but significant effort to maintain commercial shipping routes through this strategically vital waterway, even as geopolitical tensions in the region remain elevated.

cards.headline: China exports surveillance technology and state control ideology abroad
cards.teaser: After perfecting domestic surveillance systems over decades, China is promoting both the technology and the ideology of state control to other countries.
cards.body:
China has developed extensive surveillance capabilities within its borders over several decades. The country is now exporting both the technology and the governing philosophy behind its surveillance state to other nations.

The effort represents an expansion of China's influence beyond traditional diplomatic and economic channels. Countries adopting Chinese surveillance systems also receive the framework for how to use such technology for state control.

hero.headline: Blast at explosives storage site in Myanmar kills dozens
hero.body:
More than 45 people were killed and around 70 injured in an explosion at a building storing mining explosives in northeast Myanmar. The blast occurred in a village held by rebel forces.

Rescuers responded to the scene after the explosion destroyed the explosives storage facility. The building had been used to store materials for mining operations.

The death toll reflects one of the deadliest single incidents in the region in recent months. Myanmar has been in turmoil since a military coup in 2021, with armed resistance groups controlling parts of the country.

The explosion took place in territory controlled by rebel forces opposing the military government. Northeast Myanmar has seen fighting between the military and various ethnic armed organizations and resistance groups.

Rescue operations continued as workers searched for additional casualties. The explosion caused significant damage to the storage building and surrounding structures.

The exact cause of the blast has not been determined. Mining explosives are volatile materials that require careful storage and handling to prevent accidental detonation.

Myanmar's civil conflict has complicated emergency response capabilities across much of the country. Areas under rebel control often lack the infrastructure and resources available in government-held territories.

The incident adds to the civilian toll from Myanmar's ongoing internal conflict, which has displaced hundreds of thousands of people since the military seized power.

cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized the historic fortress in southern Lebanon as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a deeper ground operation against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with northern Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu characterized the seizure as a "decisive shift" in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah, stating that "we returned stronger than ever."

The castle holds deep symbolic weight for both nations. Israel previously occupied the strategic position during its extended military presence in southern Lebanon. The current capture suggests Israel intends to maintain an extended presence in the region as its offensive expands.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 arrested in France after Champions League riots
cards.teaser: Clashes with police during Champions League events resulted in hundreds of arrests and more than 200 injuries, including dozens of officers.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following clashes between crowds and police during Champions League events in France. The violence resulted in 219 injuries overall, with 57 of those being police officers.

The disorder spread across multiple locations where football fans had gathered, prompting a significant police response to control the unrest.

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election testing left against far-right
cards.teaser: Polls closed in an election that could reshape Colombia's relations with the United States after months of tension between the current president and Washington.
cards.body:
Colombian voters cast ballots in the first round of a presidential election viewed as a referendum on outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro's policies. The vote presents a stark choice between candidates with competing visions for the country's future, particularly regarding peace efforts a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

The election comes amid months of public tension between Petro and US President Donald Trump over policy differences. The outcome could significantly reshape Colombia's relationship with the United States, depending on which candidate prevails among the pro-Trump alternatives and traditional conservative contenders.

cards.headline: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection
cards.teaser: Two cases under investigation would mark the first Ebola infections outside Africa since the outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection. If confirmed, these would be the first cases detected outside Africa since the current outbreak began in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Ebola is a severe viral disease that spreads through contact with bodily fluids. The outbreak in central Africa has prompted the World Health Organization to call for community cooperation to contain the virus, particularly in the DRC's eastern regions where residents have raised concerns about medical protocols for handling victims' bodies.

cards.teaser: After perfecting domestic surveillance systems over decades, China is promoting both the technology and the ideology of state control to other countries.

China has developed extensive surveillance capabilities within its borders over several decades. The country is now exporting both the technology and the governing philosophy behind its surveillance state to other nations.

The effort represents an expansion of China's influence beyond traditional diplomatic and economic channels. Countries adopting Chinese surveillance systems also receive the framework for how to use such technology for state control.

cards.headline: Dead whale towed to shore in Denmark for autopsy
cards.teaser: A whale known as Timmy was found dead off the Danish coast after multiple rescue attempts failed to save the animal.
cards.body:
Danish authorities brought the carcass of a humpback whale to shore for an autopsy. The whale, nicknamed "Timmy" by German media, had been found dead off the coast of Anholt after drifting near Danish waters for two weeks.

Rescue teams had made multiple attempts to save the whale before it died. The autopsy will help determine the cause of death and provide insights into the whale's health and environment.

cards.headline: Pence calls Trump anti-weaponization fund deeply offensive
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized the Trump administration's $1.8 billion fund and called for it to be eliminated.
cards.body:
Mike Pence described the Trump administration's anti-weaponization fund as deeply offensive and said it should be dropped. The fund totals $1.8 billion and has drawn criticism from multiple quarters.

The fund has sparked alarm inside the White House, according to reports. Congress faces questions about what actions it can and cannot take to limit the payout fund. A list of potential applicants to the fund has begun to emerge.

cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized a strategic fortress in Lebanon during an expanding military campaign against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured the 12th-century Beaufort Castle, a strategic fortress overlooking southern Lebanon and northern Israel, as part of an expanding ground offensive against Hezbollah. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the seizure as a "decisive shift" in the military campaign.

The operation signals Israel's intention to maintain an extended military presence in Lebanon. The castle capture marks an escalation of Israeli ground operations in the region.

cards.headline: Senator Graham Platner's wife flagged sexually explicit texts to campaign
cards.teaser: The Maine Senate candidate's wife previously disclosed his extramarital sexting to his campaign staff.
cards.body:
I notice the BBC News source provided is about Marc Bolland and youth unemployment—a completely different story unrelated to Senator Graham Platner.

Since the only relevant source is The Guardian article about the Platner Senate campaign, here's the rewritten card:

---

Senator Cory Booker expressed concerns about Graham Platner's Maine Senate campaign following reports that Platner sent sexually explicit messages to women while married. Booker said Platner has "questions to answer" and that the campaign process should address the revelations.

Platner's wife had flagged the sexually explicit texts to his Senate campaign. The situation has drawn scrutiny from within Democratic circles as the Senate race continues.

cards.headline: Trump considers MAGA rally after musicians drop out of Freedom 250 concert
cards.teaser: President Trump floated holding a political rally after several artists withdrew from the Washington celebration.
cards.body:
President Trump suggested replacing the Freedom 250 concert with a "Make America Great Again" rally after multiple artists withdrew from the White House-linked event. The Great American State Fair was scheduled to take place in Washington, D.C.

Country singer Martina McBride was among the headliners who pulled out of the celebration. Following the departures, Trump proposed holding a rally instead of continuing with the concert format.

cards.headline: United flight to Spain returns over Bluetooth device name
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight to Spain reversed course and returned to Newark after a passenger's Bluetooth device raised security concerns.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight 236 diverted back to Newark late Saturday, about an hour after departing for Palma de Mallorca, Spain. The return was prompted by security concerns related to a Bluetooth device name visible to passengers and crew on the aircraft.

Crew members repeatedly asked passengers to disable their Bluetooth connections during the incident. The specific device name that triggered the security response has not been publicly disclosed, though air traffic audio and social media accounts from passengers documented the diversion.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes Ending Climate Disclosure Rule for Public Companies
cards.teaser: The regulation would have required publicly traded companies to report significant climate-related risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed eliminating a climate change disclosure rule that would have required all publicly traded companies to report whether they faced significant risks from climate change and its effects.

The regulation represented an attempt to standardize how companies inform investors about climate-related financial risks. Public companies would have been required to assess and disclose their exposure to climate change impacts on their business operations.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Returns After Bluetooth Device Name Triggers Alert
cards.teaser: A flight bound for Spain turned around midair after crew members spotted a concerning Bluetooth network name.
cards.body:
United Airlines Flight 236 from Newark to Palma de Mallorca diverted back to Newark on Saturday night, approximately an hour after takeoff. The crew had become concerned about a Bluetooth device signal detected onboard and repeatedly asked passengers to turn off their Bluetooth devices.

According to passengers who posted about the incident on social media, the Bluetooth network name itself raised security concerns that prompted the aircraft to turn around. The specific name and details about which device was responsible remain undisclosed.

cards.headline: China's Drug Development Growth Raises Concerns About U.S. Dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international cancer conference as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China are receiving significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, underscoring the country's expanding influence in pharmaceutical development. China's growing biotechnology sector is reshaping the landscape of global drug research and cancer treatment innovation.

The rise of Chinese biotech capabilities has sparked concerns among U.S. officials and industry observers about America's competitive position in the field. The prominence of Chinese clinical trials at major medical conferences reflects a meaningful shift in where cutting-edge pharmaceutical research and development is increasingly taking place.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Earns $82 Million From Young Theater Audiences
cards.teaser: The low-budget horror movie from a 20-year-old filmmaker drew strong ticket sales, suggesting young viewers will attend theaters for appealing content.
cards.body:
The horror film Backrooms generated $82 million in ticket sales, demonstrating that young audiences will go to movie theaters for content that appeals to them. The film cost $10 million to produce and came from a 20-year-old filmmaker.

The box office performance adds to evidence that younger moviegoers have not abandoned theaters entirely, despite shifts in how people consume entertainment. The success of the low-budget production shows that production costs do not necessarily determine audience turnout.

cards.headline: All-Electric Aircraft Completes Test Flight in New York City
cards.teaser: A new electric aircraft conducted a demonstration flight, offering a look at potential changes in air transportation.
cards.body:
A new all-electric aircraft made a test flight in New York City, providing a demonstration of emerging aviation technology. The flight represents development in electric-powered flight systems.

The test flight showcases ongoing efforts to develop alternatives to traditional fuel-powered aircraft. Electric aviation technology faces challenges including battery weight, range limitations, and charging infrastructure before it can be widely adopted for commercial passenger service.

cards.headline: Airbnb Expands Beyond Home Rentals to Include Cars, Groceries, and Hotels
cards.teaser: The home-sharing platform has added car rentals, groceries, and hotels to its service offerings.
cards.body:
Airbnb recently expanded its platform to include car rentals, groceries, and hotels, moving beyond its original home-sharing model. Brian Chesky, the co-founder and chief executive, continues to explore ways to redesign the service.

The additions represent a significant shift in Airbnb's business strategy. The company originally built its business on connecting travelers with people renting out their homes or spare rooms, but now competes directly with traditional hotel booking platforms and car rental services.

hero.headline: Apple plans smart glasses for late 2027
hero.body:
Apple is developing smart glasses with a planned launch in late 2027, according to reports. The company aims to enter the consumer eyewear market with an approach similar to its Apple Watch strategy.

The project represents Apple's effort to disrupt the glasses market through its own hardware design. Multiple outlets reported the timeline, with some sources indicating a Vision Air product could follow by 2029.

The glasses would compete directly with Meta's existing smart eyewear products. Industry observers have characterized Meta's current offerings as raising privacy concerns, a distinction Apple may seek to exploit in its marketing.

Apple has not publicly confirmed the product or timeline. The company typically declines to comment on future releases until formal announcements.

The development follows Apple's 2023 launch of the Vision Pro headset, a mixed reality device priced at $3,499 that targeted professional and early adopter markets. That product received mixed reception due to its high cost and limited initial software library.

Smart glasses represent a different market segment than headsets. They are designed for all-day wear and typically offer augmented reality features overlaid on the real world, rather than full immersion. Current products in the category include Meta's Ray-Ban partnership and Snap's Spectacles.

The late 2027 timeline would give Apple more than a year to refine the technology and build developer support. The Apple Watch launched in 2015 after years of development and became the best-selling smartwatch globally within two years.

Industry analysts view the eyewear category as a potential growth area for tech companies. Glasses offer a more socially acceptable form factor than headsets for daily use, though technical challenges include battery life, display technology, and heat management in a compact design.

Apple's entry could accelerate mainstream adoption of smart glasses if the company can deliver a compelling user experience at a reasonable price point. The Watch strategy involved initially positioning the device as a luxury item before expanding to broader health and fitness use cases.

cards.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 set for October launch
cards.teaser: The game will feature a campaign set during a present-day Korean war and will be available on Nintendo Switch 2.
cards.body:
Activision announced Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will launch on October 23, featuring campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ modes. The game marks the series' first appearance on Nintendo Switch 2.

The campaign centers on a modern Korean conflict scenario. Infinity Ward describes the title as grounded in military authenticity, positioning it as a return to the series' more controversial roots after years focused on melodrama. The publisher has detailed multiple editions and pre-order benefits for the fall release.

cards.headline: Nintendo reveals June game lineup for Switch consoles
cards.teaser: The company showcased 11 titles coming to both Switch 1 and Switch 2 platforms next month, including a Zelda remake.
cards.body:
Nintendo presented its game releases for June 2026 during a recent Direct presentation. The lineup includes 11 titles that will work on both the original Switch and the newer Switch 2 hardware.

A Zelda remake was among the announcements, which multiple outlets described as massive. Nintendo also revealed new Switch 2 hardware during the presentation. The June slate represents six games that observers characterized as must-play titles for the newer console.

cards.headline: Chinese startup tests reusable rocket engine
cards.teaser: Mega Engine Technology successfully fired an oxygen-rich staged-combustion engine designed for reusable rockets.
cards.body:
Mega Engine Technology, a Chinese startup co-founded in early 2024 by MIT PhD holder Zhang Chenxing in Xi'an, completed a test firing of a reusable rocket engine. The company developed high-pressure oxygen-rich staged-combustion technology, which had previously existed almost entirely within state-run propulsion facilities in China.

The engine uses oxygen-rich staged combustion, a design approach also employed by SpaceX. Multiple outlets described the test as an advance in Chinese private space capabilities and characterized the engine as suitable for deep space missions. The startup achieved the milestone within roughly two years of its founding.

cards.headline: Artist KC Green settles with AI startup over meme use
cards.teaser: The creator of the This is fine comic reached an agreement with Artisan after the company used the image in advertisements.
cards.body:
KC Green, creator of the popular This is fine meme, has reached a settlement with AI startup Artisan following the unauthorized use of his comic in advertising materials. The company has removed the advertisements in question.

The This is fine image, which shows a dog sitting in a burning room, has become one of the internet's most recognizable illustrations since its original publication.

cards.headline: Two top weekend films directed by former YouTubers
cards.teaser: Both of the biggest movie releases were helmed by directors who started their careers making videos for YouTube.
cards.body:
The two highest-performing films at the box office were both directed by individuals who began as YouTube content creators. The releases represent a continued trend of YouTubers transitioning into traditional filmmaking.

Observers described the YouTube to prestige horror pipeline as looking very strong based on the weekend results. The success of both films suggests audiences are receptive to work from directors who built their initial followings through online video platforms rather than conventional film school or studio apprenticeship routes.

cards.headline: Pixel Watch 5 reportedly found in ocean
cards.teaser: Someone claimed to have discovered an unreleased Google smartwatch while in the ocean.
cards.body:
An individual reported finding what appears to be a Pixel Watch 5 in the ocean. Google has not announced the device, making the discovery notable if verified.

The circumstances of how an unreleased product ended up in the ocean were not explained in available reports. Google typically maintains strict security around upcoming hardware releases, making pre-launch discoveries rare. The company has not commented on the reported find.

hero.headline: Virat Kohli leads Royal Challengers Bengaluru to second straight IPL title
hero.body:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeated Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the Indian Premier League final, securing back-to-back titles. Virat Kohli scored an unbeaten 75 to guide his team to victory in the match played in Ahmedabad.

Kohli's innings proved decisive as Bengaluru chased down their target against the home team. The performance marked a significant achievement for the franchise, which had never won the IPL until their breakthrough last season.

Bengaluru's bowling attack played a crucial role in the victory, with their seamers outperforming Gujarat's bowlers despite playing in Gujarat's home stadium. The bowling performance set up the successful chase that followed.

Kohli delivered the title-winning stroke to complete the victory. The win represents the fulfillment of a long-held ambition for the star batsman, who had previously come close to IPL glory multiple times before finally breaking through last year.

The triumph extends Bengaluru's reign as IPL champions and establishes them as the dominant force in Indian cricket's premier Twenty20 competition. Gujarat Titans, playing in front of their home crowd in Ahmedabad, were unable to overcome Bengaluru's all-around performance.

The back-to-back titles represent a remarkable turnaround for a franchise that had built a reputation for falling short in crucial matches. Kohli's leadership and batting form have been central to the team's transformation into champions.

Bengaluru's bowlers set the tone by restricting Gujarat to a manageable total before Kohli took control with the bat. His unbeaten knock ensured there were no late stumbles in the chase, with Bengaluru crossing the finish line with wickets in hand.

The victory completes a dream season for Kohli and Bengaluru, cementing their status as the team to beat in the IPL.

cards.headline: Jonas Vingegaard completes cycling Grand Tour sweep with Giro d'Italia win
cards.teaser: Jonas Vingegaard became the eighth rider to win all three men's Grand Tours with his victory in the Giro d'Italia.
cards.body:
Jonas Vingegaard won the Giro d'Italia, completing victories across all three of cycling's Grand Tours. The Danish rider finished with a margin of five minutes and 22 seconds, securing the overall title after the final flat stage into Rome.

Vingegaard is now the eighth cyclist to win the Giro, Tour de France, and Vuelta a España, joining an elite group that includes Bernard Hinault, Eddy Merckx, and Vincenzo Nibali. He will now focus on the Tour de France in July, where he faces his biggest rival Tadej Pogacar.

cards.headline: Alex Palou wins fourth IndyCar race of season at Detroit Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Alex Palou secured his fourth victory of the IndyCar season at the Detroit Grand Prix after navigating through a race filled with incidents.
cards.body:
Alex Palou claimed victory at the Detroit Grand Prix, securing his fourth win of the 2026 IndyCar season. Starting from pole position, Palou navigated a chaotic race filled with incidents and strategic challenges to cross the finish line first.

The win extends Palou's lead in the IndyCar championship standings, continuing his dominant stretch through the season.

cards.headline: Liverpool to begin talks with Andoni Iraola for head coach position
cards.teaser: Liverpool will open formal negotiations with Andoni Iraola this week as they search for a new head coach.
cards.body:
Liverpool will hold formal talks with Andoni Iraola this week about their managerial vacancy. The club is moving swiftly through their search for a new head coach and intends to speak with preferred candidates immediately. Iraola, currently managing in the Premier League, is the frontrunner for the role.

Liverpool also plan to sound out other candidates including Stuttgart's Sebastian Hoeness and Pierre Sage of Lens. The club hopes to appoint Arne Slot's successor before the World Cup begins.

cards.headline: Max Burgin wins 800 meters at Diamond League meet in Morocco
cards.teaser: Great Britain's Max Burgin powered clear of a world-class field to win the 800 meters at the Diamond League meeting in Morocco.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Max Burgin claimed victory in the 800 meters at the Diamond League meeting in Rabat, Morocco, powering clear of a world-class field to secure the win. He defeated Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi of Kenya in what was described as a "special" race.

The performance represents one of the biggest wins of Burgin's career, showcasing his strength as a middle-distance runner on the global stage.

cards.headline: United States defeats Senegal 3-2 in World Cup warm-up friendly
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team beat Senegal 3-2 in a pre-World Cup friendly match.
cards.body:
Christian Pulisic ended a six-month scoring drought as the United States defeated Senegal 3-2 in a friendly match in Charlotte, North Carolina. Sergiño Dest opened the scoring early in the first half, before Pulisic assisted on another goal and scored himself to help the USMNT take control of the match.

The victory marks a turnaround for the US team following recent losses to Belgium and Portugal. The friendly served as preparation for the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, with another tune-up match against Germany scheduled for June 6 in Chicago.

cards.headline: FIFA to ban goalkeeper tactical timeouts at 2026 World Cup
cards.teaser: Players at the 2026 World Cup will be prohibited from going to the technical area to speak with coaches during goalkeeper injury stoppages.
cards.body:
FIFA will prohibit players from visiting the technical area to consult with coaches during goalkeeper injury treatment at the 2026 World Cup. The rule change targets the practice of teams using these stoppages as informal timeouts to receive tactical instructions from the sideline.

The regulation addresses concerns that goalkeeper injuries have been exploited as opportunities for strategic discussions between players and coaching staff.

hero.headline: Kelly Curtis, Actress and Sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, Dies at 69
hero.body:
Kelly Curtis, an actress and the older sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, has died at age 69. Jamie Lee Curtis confirmed the death in a touching tribute shared on social media.

In her public message, Jamie Lee Curtis described her sister as her first friend and lifelong confidant. She shared previously unpublished photos alongside her tribute and expressed how much she missed Kelly.

Kelly Curtis had a career in the entertainment industry, appearing in various film and television roles. She was the daughter of legendary actors Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh, placing her within a prominent Hollywood family. Her younger sister Jamie Lee Curtis went on to become one of the most recognizable actresses in cinema, known for her roles in horror films like Halloween and dramatic performances in projects such as Everything Everywhere All at Once.

While Jamie Lee Curtis achieved widespread fame and critical acclaim throughout her career, Kelly Curtis maintained a more private public presence. She worked steadily in entertainment but chose not to seek the same level of spotlight as her sister.

The family's connection to Hollywood spans generations. Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh were major stars of classic cinema, establishing the Curtis name as part of entertainment history. Jamie Lee Curtis has continued that legacy, becoming an award-winning performer who works across multiple genres.

In her tribute, Jamie Lee Curtis emphasized the personal bond she shared with her sister rather than focusing on professional details. She highlighted their relationship from childhood through adulthood, underscoring how central Kelly was to her life. The sisters remained close throughout the years, with their connection extending beyond their shared family background in the entertainment world.

The cause of Kelly Curtis's death has not been disclosed publicly. Jamie Lee Curtis's statement serves as the primary acknowledgment of her sister's passing, with the actress choosing to mark the loss through a personal and intimate social media post rather than through a formal announcement.

Jamie Lee Curtis has not released information about funeral arrangements or provided further details surrounding the circumstances of her sister's death. Her public tribute appears to be the main way the family has chosen to honor Kelly Curtis's memory at this time.

The loss represents a significant moment for one of Hollywood's most established families. The Curtis family has maintained a presence in the entertainment industry for decades, with multiple generations contributing to film and television. Kelly Curtis's passing marks the end of an era for those who grew up watching the family navigate their lives in the public eye.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa Marries Callum Turner in London Ceremony
cards.teaser: The pop star wed the actor in an intimate ceremony at Old Marylebone Town Hall.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa married actor Callum Turner during a ceremony at Old Marylebone Town Hall in London. The wedding took place on Sunday.

The ceremony was described as intimate, suggesting a small guest list. Old Marylebone Town Hall is a historic venue in central London that has hosted numerous celebrity weddings over the years.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Delivers Freestyle Dissing Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj at Roots Picnic
cards.teaser: The rapper performed a surprise a cappella freestyle on Saturday targeting several high-profile artists.
cards.body:
Jay-Z delivered an a cappella freestyle at the Roots Picnic that included disses aimed at Drake, Kanye West, and Nicki Minaj. The performance took place on Saturday and was described as fiery.

The freestyle was unannounced, catching attendees by surprise. Jay-Z performed without musical backing, delivering his verses a cappella at the Philadelphia music festival.

cards.headline: Backrooms Opens With $81 Million, Breaking YouTuber Box Office Records
cards.teaser: The film drew Gen Z audiences and marked another success for YouTuber-driven content in theaters.
cards.body:
Backrooms debuted with $81 million to $82 million in ticket sales, setting a new record for films tied to YouTuber creators. The horror film drew young moviegoers to theaters in unprecedented numbers.

The success follows strong performance from Obsession, another YouTuber-associated film that saw unusual box office gains. Industry observers suggested these results could influence future moviemaking strategies, as studios take note of the drawing power of content creators with established online audiences.

cards.headline: Cody Rhodes Retains WWE Title Against Gunther at Clash in Italy
cards.teaser: The championship match ended with Rhodes keeping his belt in what was described as a finish involving controversy.
cards.body:
Cody Rhodes defeated Gunther to retain the WWE championship at the Clash in Italy event. The match conclusion was described as ending in controversy, though Rhodes emerged as the winner.

Before the match, Gunther stated that if Rhodes did not have the approval of the people, Rhodes could not give himself that approval. The bout was highlighted as one of the main events of the international WWE show held in Italy.

cards.headline: Sydney Sweeney and Scooter Braun Spotted on Date Night in New York
cards.teaser: The actress and music executive were seen holding hands during an evening out in the city.
cards.body:
Sydney Sweeney and Scooter Braun were photographed together during a date night in New York City. The pair held hands while visiting Times Square, which Braun described as a first-time experience for the location.

Sweeney wore multiple outfits during the outing, including vintage Chanel and a plunging black dress. Braun discussed the surprise of dating Sweeney in public comments, confirming their relationship status.

cards.headline: Sol Ruca Wins WWE Women's Intercontinental Title, Ending Becky Lynch's Reign
cards.teaser: Ruca defeated Lynch at WWE Clash in Italy following controversy at a previous event.
cards.body:
Sol Ruca won the WWE Women's Intercontinental Championship by defeating Becky Lynch at WWE Clash in Italy. The title change came after a situation involving controversy at Saturday Night's Main Event.

Lynch's loss broke an unfortunate record, though the specific nature of the record was not detailed. Ruca reacted publicly to recent concerns about her health following the victory.

hero.headline: Congress returns to unresolved immigration and Iran oversight disputes
hero.teaser: Lawmakers face the same stalled issues they left before the holiday break.
hero.body:
Congress returns with immigration funding, a Justice Department fund dispute, and Iran war oversight questions still unresolved. Lawmakers left for Memorial Day break without making progress on any of the three issues.

The immigration enforcement funding package remains stalled. Questions about congressional oversight of the Iran war also await resolution when members return to Washington.

cards.headline: Senator says Iran stronger after three months of US war
cards.teaser: Sen.
cards.body:
Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) said Iran has grown stronger during the three-month conflict with the US, citing the country's use of drones and its impact on regional shipping. The senator, who serves on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, made the assessment during a television interview, marking a public critique of the war's effectiveness.

The conflict has coincided with significant economic pressures at home. US inflation hit its fastest pace in three years in April, driven by higher energy prices linked to the Iran war. The rising cost of living has eroded household purchasing power and sparked growing frustration with the administration's handling of the economy. Meanwhile, reports suggest ceasefire negotiations may be underway.

cards.headline: Republicans stall on reconciliation bill and surveillance extension
cards.teaser: Internal GOP disputes leave two major legislative items unresolved.
cards.body:
Republicans left Washington last week without resolving disputes over an immigration enforcement funding package and an extension of warrantless spying powers. The intraparty conflicts have persisted for a month.

The reconciliation bill and FISA extension both remain stalled. Republican lawmakers are no closer to agreement on either matter than they were before Memorial Day break.

cards.headline: DNC chair faces pressure over election autopsy and finances
cards.teaser: Ken Martin confronts growing criticism as Democrats look toward 2028.
cards.body:
DNC chair Ken Martin is facing a crisis of confidence among Democrats over the committee's handling of the 2024 election autopsy and its financial problems. The dispute represents the biggest early test of party leadership heading into the 2028 presidential race.

Martin has so far prevented a revolt among DNC members. The conflict is unfolding as the committee sets the calendar for the 2028 presidential primary.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump health memo three days after checkup
cards.teaser: A summary issued late Friday night concluded the president is in excellent health.
cards.body:
The White House released a memo from Dr. Sean Barbabella summarizing President Trump's recent checkup at Walter Reed Military Medical Center. According to the memo, Trump remains in excellent health with strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function.

The memo noted Trump has lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising. The findings were released Friday night, three days after his Tuesday examination.

cards.headline: Former Biden aides criticize Jill Biden's new book
cards.teaser: Many view the memoir as rewriting history and unhelpful to Democrats.
cards.body:
Former Biden aides told Axios they view Jill Biden's new book as rewriting history, unhelpful to the Democratic Party, and tone-deaf. The criticism followed the appearance of excerpts from "View from the West Wing: A Memoir" online and the former first lady's first interview since her husband left office in January 2025.

Most Democratic Party leaders do not want to discuss Joe Biden's presidency. Both Bidens are writing books, making that difficult.

cards.headline: Pence says effort underway to rewrite Jan. 6 history
cards.teaser: The former vice president expressed confidence in how history will judge his role.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said there has clearly been an effort to rewrite the history of the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. He made the comments during a television interview.

Pence said he is confident about the judgment of history regarding his role and that of Republicans and Democrats who returned to the Capitol that day after the police response.
